blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: Scope — The part of a program in which a variable can be accessed.
Local variable — A variable visible only within the method or block where it is declared.
Global variable — A variable that can be accessed from multiple parts of a program.
Parameter — The named input in a method definition.
Argument — The actual value or variable supplied in a method call.
Pass by value — Passing a copy so changes inside the method do not change the original variable.

blocks.title: Scope controls where a variable can be used
blocks.text: A local variable is declared inside a method or block and can only be used within that scope. For this course, we use a class-level static field to demonstrate the OCR idea of a global variable that can be accessed by multiple methods.

blocks.title: Parameters are local to the method
blocks.text: A parameter receives data when a method is called and behaves as a local variable inside that method. number exists within Triple . The value supplied in the call is the argument.

blocks.title: By value = the method receives a copy
blocks.text: Changing number changes only the method's local copy. The original variable in Main() is unchanged.

blocks.title: ref gives access to the original variable
blocks.text: Write ref in both places: in the method parameter and in the method call.
